Trading on 'fundamentals' seems easy, but what do you do when revenue starts dropping like this?

1) Hold
2) Sell
3) Buy the dip

Ok but consider that the token trades at 0.61x annualized fees and 1.22x annualized holder revenue.

Buy more? Yet these metrics are based on the last 30 days. Protocol is new.

But what if it belongs to a crypto category which historically is very cyclical, loses attention and gets flooded with new competitors?

Still 'cheap' valuation yet only if the PROTOCOL and revenue survive.

Yeah, trading the revenue meta looks easy when revenue only goes up.

But you still need to bet on:

1) The sector continuing to grow
2) The team continuing to ship
3) Degens continuing to trade
4) Competitors not taking its market share

The revenue is visible onchain in real time but decision to trade is still tough.

The White House seems to be passing the diesel hot potato to the states — and some of them are acting (and I expect that many more would follow).

Yesterday, Texas announced it will allow the use of so-called “dyed diesel” on its roads. Dyed diesel is like normal diesel but cheaper because much lower taxation (and typically it can only be used for farming, construction and other non-road uses).

The measure would save Texas truckers the 24.4 cents-a-gallon federal excise tax plus another 20 cents from Texas state tax. But, importantly from a political stand point, the measure doesn’t lower diesel cost to farmers, which already have access to untaxed dyed diesel. 

Other states have higher state diesel taxes (the national average for the state tax is 35.5 per gallon), suggesting that the measure could reduce diesel prices for road uses  (mostly freight) by ~60 cents per gallon across the country if all states implement it. 

(By allowing the use of dyed diesel, the White House / state governors can fast track the tax relief in a much faster way that trying to suspend the federal and state fuel duties, which would require legislature approval. It’s a tax loophole)

tweets.text:
Hmmm... seems like everyone is adopting Venice's VVV <> DIEM tokenomics rn

First it's Orbio on RHC

Now it's the entire Bittensor subnets eco

Burn Alpha tokens, Get Gamma tokens — tokenized usage credits that tied to specific subnets goods & services

I mean this is great utility for the token as it adds on deflationary mechanic to it BUT if everyone is doing it, then...

> It becomes harder to scale the tokenized credits market as there's gonna be too much supply fighting for limited demand

This is great for inference buyers but not so great for sellers as they have to push down the price

AND since Venice has already dominated the tokenized inference credit market to a degree, it's gonna be tough competing with DIEM

I would very much rather have the tokenized usage credits go into the same token instead of creating a new one, just like what Dolphin have planned with POD

Nonetheless, it's an exciting/positive update for Bittensor. 

Will be interesting to see how the secondary market dynamic plays out beyond inference subnets

https://t.co/OXMnZMckZY
